chat.text: :bike::hut:

chat.text: forward is fine

chat.text: Does it save us a bit on SUBSCRIBE changing the default?

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: have FORWARD and PAUSED :)

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: i.e. if we move to PAUSED?

chat.author: Magnus Westerlund
chat.text: Minutes: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/minutes-interim-2026-moq-25-202610141600/

chat.author: Jordi Cenzano
chat.text: @magnus Your mic is breaking (at least for me). Could you lower a bit the mic level

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: I just made THESE AI notes much more confusing

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: If you can cache Gone then you could get Gone from a relay

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: Not exclusive to OP, right?

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: Ah, I'm not sure why a relay would want to invent a Gone it didn't receive

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: +1 on clarifying the PR on Gone a bit more

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: that is a terrible use case

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: track names are cheap

chat.author: Mo Zanaty
chat.text: At the interim, people preferred app compression (track name/prop) over tranport compression (like transfer-encoding).

chat.author: Michal Hošna
chat.text: I couldn't come up with MTI that cannot be better implemented as hop-to-hop extension communicated in SETUP.

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: @mo right . Don't remember what we decided on that

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: +1 to Alan

chat.author: Ian Swett
chat.text: SHOULD NOT

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: SHOULD NOT is fine

chat.author: Steven Riedl
chat.text: I would prefer MUST NOT, data that needs to change should be on a seperate track.

chat.author: Steven Riedl
chat.text: two relays could change differently

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: MUST NOT interacts weirdly with incomplete caches maybe

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: what Mo is saying

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: Flip side: updating poses a risk for anything that wants signatures over properties

chat.author: Mo Zanaty
chat.text: @Mike, immutable

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: @mike yes, it will atleast help to find out where the things went wrong .. adding things you care abut in to e2e auth is good designr egardless

chat.author: Steven Riedl
chat.text: yup 0x0b immutable...

chat.author: Steven Riedl
chat.text: so , could go either, still like MUST

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: IMO, Mostly the immutability of objects is in the draft has implications for what relays can do that won't break applications that follow the rules. Gives relays more freedom, e.g. to cache.

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: +1 to ALan on Immutable the way it is defined

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: *is in the draft _because it has_

chat.author: Steven Riedl
chat.text: Both cases fit the existing split: anything signed goes in Immutable Properties (0xB), which relays MUST NOT touch, and SHOULD NOT on the mutable list leaves room to fill an incomplete cache. Works for me.

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: I think I see what Mo is saying about it being mostly up to applications to enforce immutability though

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: immutabel blob needs to traverse end to end with no modifications . The drfat prvides way for relays to not adjust it , but add things around it

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: this is important for any e2ee framework to be simple to design comapred to have an index of some sorts telling where in payload one needs to pick and choose the things that contribute to AAD .. Victor's idea as it is today is simple to implement though

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: What are expectations about early objects with FORWARD=1 / PAUSED=0 ?

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: it can be cached if the relay can do it .. if not, it will send req_ok with paused=1

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: This capability requires a security analysis that cannot happen in this call. Namespaces are tied to authentication

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: You should probably somehow authenticate the relay you're choosing to connect to in the first place... but yeah CORS is a good place to look for relevant ideas.

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: say security cameras need to publish the feed even if there are no downstream subscribers yet . its applications and relay work together

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: :tada:

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: LOL

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: end of end of group bit???

chat.author: Steven Riedl
chat.text: B

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: 3 B of overhead on a multi-object stream is negligible

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: I think Mutable EOG is a defensible design but it's a big change to the object model

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: I'm not sure how/where you'd draw the line for hop by hop EODG. What if you get more objects on other streams?

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: I don't think we should open this up to ask if EOG is useful. This is a discussion about compressing the signal

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: I can see value of end to end "as minted" EOG signals (signaled however), but I'm not quite sure what we win by inventing a new EODG thing

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: C seems like a reasonable compromise. Only keep it for the case where the compression might matter?

chat.author: Suhas Nandakumar
chat.text: +1 to filter not applyting to status objects. thats a cleaner design and explicit

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: +1 Martin

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: I like C because it also resolves many of the implementation edge cases

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: There is still a "never use datagrams, just make single-object-streams and cancel/timeout" camp, so I think D may not fly.

chat.author: Ian Swett
chat.text: Single Object Subgroups are sort of special

chat.author: Steven Riedl
chat.text: switch to the header bit I guess

chat.author: Mike English
chat.text: For a while we were intentionally a bit ambiguous about whether object payloads needed to be byte identical or if equivalence was an application-determined property. I know we tightened that up, but I don't remember where/when.
